1vd-read.check: A box plot generally cannot determine the exact mean or sample size. Whiskers may show extrema or a specified outlier convention; use the chart legend.

2vd-predict.entry: If the displayed fitted line is y=2.5x+10, enter f(x)=2.5x+10 then f(8). If only a drawn line is supplied, use two points on that line to estimate its equation.
2vd-predict.check: Do not refit the observed dots when the question asks about the given fit. Label extrapolation outside the observed input range as less supported.

2vd-model.entry: Put data in x_1,y_1. Enter y_1~m x_1+b for linear and, for positive-response growth data, y_1~a*b^(x_1). Compare predictions and residual patterns.
2vd-model.check: A small residual alone does not establish an appropriate model. Use shape, units, positive exponential base, and the question’s intended family; avoid extrapolating wildly.

2vd-slope.entry: For a fitted model W=1.8t+12, compute W(t+1)-W(t)=1.8. If t is weeks and W is grams, say predicted increase of 1.8 grams per week.
2vd-slope.check: Association is not proof of causation. If t measures decades or hundreds of units, one input unit represents that full scale.

2vd-rate.entry: Enter f(x)=x^2+1, then (f(5)-f(2))/(5-2)=7. For a graph use the stated endpoint outputs in the same quotient.
2vd-rate.check: Endpoints must have different x-values. This is the average rate over an interval, not necessarily a tangent slope or a constant rate throughout.

2vd-read.entry: Draw a small checklist of x range, y range, and inclusive endpoints. Count only observed plotted points meeting every condition, one vertical strip at a time.
2vd-read.check: Do not count points on a fitted line as observations. Check axes for truncated scales, overlapping observations, and whether boundaries are included.

inf-moe.entry: An estimate of 62% with margin 4 percentage points gives [58%,66%]. To assess a claim above 60%, notice this interval includes values on both sides of 60%.
inf-moe.check: This is uncertainty about the population parameter, not the range of individual responses. Larger random samples reduce expected margin under comparable design and confidence level; not every realized interval must be narrower.

inf-estimate.choose: Hand: sample proportion times eligible population
inf-estimate.entry: If 36 of 120 randomly selected residents have a feature, estimate 9000*(36/120)=2700 among 9000 residents.
inf-estimate.check: Use the population from which the sample was selected. This is an estimate, not an exact census; a convenience sample may not support population inference.

stc-general.entry: Write population -> randomly selected sample -> respondents. If students were randomly selected from one school, identify that school’s students as the potential inference population.
stc-general.check: Nonresponse and coverage can still introduce bias. Random assignment to treatments does not by itself make a sample representative of a broader population.

stc-design.entry: Make two yes/no boxes: random selection supports generalization to the sampled population; random assignment supports a causal treatment comparison under a sound experiment.
stc-design.check: An observational association alone does not establish causation. Volunteer sampling may be biased; it does not guarantee a particular direction or magnitude of bias.

av-area.entry: For a 10-by-8 rectangle with a right-triangle notch of legs 3 and 4, enter 10*8-(1/2)*3*4=74. For a circle with diameter 10 use pi*(10/2)^2.
av-area.check: Use perpendicular height for a triangle and square units for area. Subtract only removed, nonoverlapping pieces; preserve exact pi when requested.

av-perimeter.entry: For a rectangle width w and length 2w+3, write P=2w+2(2w+3). In a composite figure, trace each exposed boundary segment once.
av-perimeter.check: Shared interior edges are not perimeter. For a removed corner, added notch edges can replace equal lengths; area change alone does not determine perimeter change.

av-volume.choose: Desmos: inverse volume with a positive domain
av-volume.entry: For a cylinder of radius 3 and volume 90pi, enter 90*pi/(pi*3^2) to find height 10. For sphere radius from volume V, use (3V/(4pi))^(1/3).
av-volume.check: Use the correct solid’s factor, and positive physical dimensions. If a diagram gives diameter, halve it before squaring or cubing; keep exact units.

av-surface.entry: For an open-top box length 5, width 3, height 2, enter 5*3+2*5*2+2*3*2=47. List the base and four side faces before adding.
av-surface.check: Surface area uses square units. Include only exposed faces named by the question; a cylinder may require zero, one, or two circular ends.

av-scale.entry: If similar shapes have area ratio 9:25, their positive length factor is sqrt(25/9)=5/3; volume factor is (5/3)^3=125/27.
av-scale.check: Area and volume power rules require uniform similarity. Changing only one dimension uses only that dimension’s factor, not k^2 or k^3.

lat-parallel.choose: Hand: reduce to one acute angle
lat-parallel.entry: Mark an angle theta at one crossing. Vertical and corresponding angles copy theta; adjacent straight-line angles become 180-theta. Label each crossing before solving.
lat-parallel.check: Corresponding and alternate angle equalities require parallel lines. Do not infer parallelism from appearance; use the stated facts or a valid converse.

lat-lines.choose: Hand: equations from a local intersection
lat-lines.entry: For adjacent angles 3x+10 and 5x-6 on a straight line, solve (3x+10)+(5x-6)=180, giving x=22. Then compute each angle.
lat-lines.check: A variable is not necessarily the requested angle. Vertical angles are opposite at the same intersection; adjacent angles are not generally equal.

lat-triangle.entry: For a triangle with angles x,2x,3x, solve 6x=180, then list 30,60,90. For a regular n-gon, each interior angle is 180(n-2)/n.
lat-triangle.check: Each triangle angle must be strictly between 0 and 180 degrees. The regular-polygon formula for each angle requires regularity, though the total formula only requires a simple polygon.

lat-similar.entry: For ABC similar to DEF, write A<->D,B<->E,C<->F and AB/DE=BC/EF=AC/DF. Use one known pair to scale every other length.
lat-similar.check: Correspondence follows the named order, even under rotation or reflection. Congruence has scale factor 1; angle equality alone does not give equal side lengths.

rtt-pythag.entry: If hypotenuse is 13 and one leg is 5, enter sqrt(13^2-5^2)=12. If the two legs are given, use sqrt(a^2+b^2).
rtt-pythag.check: Confirm the triangle is right and identify the longest side as hypotenuse. The radicand cannot be negative for a real physical length.

rtt-trig.entry: For a 30-degree angle with hypotenuse 10, enter 10*sin(30*pi/180) in radian mode, or switch to degree mode and enter 10*sin(30).
rtt-trig.check: Do not mix degree inputs with radian settings. Opposite and adjacent depend on the named angle; inverse sine returns an angle, not a side ratio.

rtt-complement.entry: In a right triangle A+B=90 degrees, so sin(A)=cos(B). If cos(B)=3/5, then sin(A)=3/5 without finding either angle.
rtt-complement.check: The inference sin(A)=cos(B) => A+B=90 degrees needs A and B acute; outside that domain periodicity produces other possibilities.

rtt-special.entry: For a 30-60-90 triangle with long leg 9, set k*sqrt(3)=9. Then short leg k=3sqrt(3) and hypotenuse 2k=6sqrt(3).
rtt-special.check: The short leg is opposite 30 degrees, not necessarily the horizontal side. Keep exact radicals when the requested form is exact.

rtt-similar.entry: For a right triangle whose altitude divides the hypotenuse into p and q, h^2=pq; each leg squared equals the full hypotenuse times its adjacent segment.
rtt-similar.check: These identities require the perpendicular altitude to the hypotenuse. Do not apply them to an arbitrary interior segment; match triangles by angle first.

cir-read.entry: For x^2+y^2-3x+5y=2, center is (3/2,-5/2) and radius squared is 2+(3/2)^2+(5/2)^2=21/2. Evaluate sqrt(21/2) only if a decimal is wanted.
cir-read.check: Centers need not be integers. First divide by a common nonzero coefficient of x^2 and y^2. Unequal squared coefficients generally do not describe a circle; radius squared must be positive for a nondegenerate real circle.

cir-build.choose: Hand: radius squared from a point
cir-build.check: Use squared distance directly: taking a square root then squaring adds rounding. Center signs reverse inside each bracket; coordinate units determine squared equation units.

cir-transform.choose: Hand: transform center and radius separately
cir-transform.entry: A circle centered at (1,-2) with r^2=5 shifted right 3 and scaled to twice the radius has center (4,-2) and r^2=20. Write (x-4)^2+(y+2)^2=20.
cir-transform.check: A translation of the circle differs from dilation about the origin, which also scales the center. Radius scale k multiplies r^2 by k^2.

cir-radians.choose: Desmos: preserve pi and state the mode
cir-radians.entry: Convert 150 degrees with 150*pi/180=5pi/6. In radian mode a unit-circle point at this angle is (cos(5*pi/6),sin(5*pi/6)).
cir-radians.check: An angle in radians is dimensionless; do not multiply by pi twice when the supplied angle already contains pi. Decimal calculator values do not replace exact requested multiples of pi.

cir-arc.choose: Hand: one angle fraction for both measures
cir-arc.entry: For radius 6 and central angle 60 degrees, arc length=(60/360)*2*pi*6=2pi and sector area=(60/360)*pi*6^2=6pi. With theta in radians use r*theta and (1/2)*r^2*theta.
cir-arc.check: Arc is length units; sector is square units. Choose the minor or major angle asked for. The radian formulas cannot take a raw degree number.

cir-tangent.entry: For center (h,k) and tangency point (p,q), write (p-h)(x-p)+(q-k)(y-q)=0. Center (1,2), point (4,2) gives x=4.
cir-tangent.check: First verify the point lies on the circle. The vector formula handles horizontal or vertical radii without division; negative-reciprocal slopes require a defined nonzero radius slope.

cir-geo.entry: Draw radii to named points on the circle and to each tangency point. Mark equal radii and the right angle between radius and tangent; then use triangle angle sums.
cir-geo.check: A central angle is twice an inscribed angle subtending the same arc. Choose the correct arc and do not assume an unmarked chord is a diameter or the drawing is to scale.

source_cases.title: Evaluate the coefficient sum with its scale
source_cases.spot: Asked for a sum of coefficients rather than each coefficient.
source_cases.hand: Evaluate at 1; multiply by 6 for efc469c4 because coefficients were divided by 6.
source_cases.calculator: Enter the original expression at 1; preserve outside scale.
source_cases.check: Answers -612, 32, 6632 respectively.

source_cases.title: Cancel structure before expanding
source_cases.spot: Shared blocks, a perfect square, signed products, or a geometric sum.
source_cases.hand: Subtract shared a first; recognize (c+d)²; distribute signed factors; telescope powers.
source_cases.calculator: A numeric substitution can reject choices; it does not establish an identity.
source_cases.check: b²-2bc+c²; (x+a)(x-a); 2x²-xy-3y²; 1-p⁷.

source_cases.title: Use a known factor as a zero
source_cases.spot: A linear factor is given and a parameter is requested.
source_cases.hand: Substitute x=k into the first polynomial. For the second, use (3x+7)(x+2b).
source_cases.calculator: Evaluate the polynomial at the stated factor root, retaining k>0 or integral b>0.
source_cases.check: n=29; middle coefficient 49 with b=7.

source_cases.title: Tangency belongs to the difference
source_cases.spot: A parabola and an oblique line intersect exactly once.
source_cases.hand: Subtract equations; repeated zero of 2x²-24x+64-a gives x=6.
source_cases.calculator: Graph both equations only after finding a=-8; inspect the common point.
source_cases.check: At x=6 both y values are 10. This is not the original parabola vertex.

source_cases.title: Strict discriminant bounds and integers
source_cases.spot: No real solution plus an integer extremum.
source_cases.hand: Set discriminant strictly below zero and then select an allowed integer.
source_cases.calculator: Use a calculator for the real bound, then check neighboring integers algebraically.
source_cases.check: 16, 51, 50, 14; equality would give one real solution. No live calculator execution claimed.

source_cases.title: Count exponential crossings by range
source_cases.spot: An increasing exponential minus a positive constant.
source_cases.hand: Base a/7>1 gives strict increase, and the range after subtracting b is (-b,infinity); zero occurs once.
source_cases.calculator: A graph at sample constants can illustrate the result; monotonicity and range prove it for every allowed constant.
source_cases.check: One crossing. a>7 and b>0 suffice; b>c is not needed.

source_cases.title: Bound integer histogram means at the allowed endpoints
source_cases.spot: Two same-shaped histograms ask for the smallest possible mean difference; each bin is lower-inclusive and upper-exclusive.
source_cases.hand: Minimize every A value and maximize every B value. A uses 20,30,40,50 with frequencies 3,4,7,9; B uses 19,29,39,49 with those frequencies. Each paired value differs by 1, so the mean difference is 1. A 10-unit shift in bin labels does not fix the raw-data mean difference at 10.
source_cases.calculator: Optional: (3*20+4*30+7*40+9*50)/23-(3*19+4*29+7*39+9*49)/23. Do not enter bin midpoints as exact observations.
source_cases.check: Integers below 20 end at 19. If the data were unrestricted real numbers, that endpoint argument would change.

source_cases.title: Use divisibility as well as the mean equation
source_cases.spot: A missing positive integer is bounded, and the final mean must itself be an integer.
source_cases.hand: Nine known values have sum 9*42=378. The tenth x must exceed 42 to raise the mean and must be below 60. Since (378+x)/10 is integral, x ends in 2. The only allowed value is 52, also the largest value in the completed set.
source_cases.calculator: Optional: (378+52)/10=43. Test constraints after solving; an unrestricted decimal solution does not meet the integer requirement.
source_cases.check: 42 would keep the mean unchanged; 62 violates the upper bound. The only valid answer is 52.

source_cases.title: Balanced outward changes preserve the sum but increase spread
source_cases.spot: An odd number of distinct values has equal mean and median; values on each side move outward by the same amount.
source_cases.hand: There are 13 values below 33 and 13 above. Subtracting 7 thirteen times and adding 7 thirteen times has net change zero, so sum and mean remain fixed. No value crosses 33, so the median remains 33. Every changed distance from the unchanged mean increases, so standard deviation increases.
source_cases.calculator: No calculation is needed. A numerical illustration may show the mechanism, but the equal counts and unchanged mean prove it for all 27 values.
source_cases.check: The distinct-values condition guarantees exactly 13 values on each side. This is not the same operation as adding 7 to every value.

source_cases.title: The sampling frame can be broader than the displayed table
source_cases.spot: A study samples one population, then displays only participants meeting a practice threshold.
source_cases.hand: For the question about the study’s largest generalization population, trace the original random selection. The trivia study samples 55 from all tournament teams, even though its table displays 40. The piano study samples 85 second-year conservatory students in one region, even though its table displays 75. Keep all original geographic and year restrictions.
source_cases.calculator: No calculator helps identify a sampling frame. Underline the sentence describing random selection before inspecting the table.
source_cases.check: Answers: all tournament teams; all second-year conservatory piano students in the specified region. A table-only conditional claim would still concern its displayed subgroup.

source_cases.title: Scale the winning margin, not just the winner’s votes
source_cases.spot: An election poll asks “by how many votes” the winner is expected to win.
source_cases.hand: The sample lead is 483-320=163 votes among 803. Expected turnout 6424 is 8 times the sample size. Scale the lead: 163*8=1304. Alternatively subtract the projected totals 3864-2560.
source_cases.calculator: Optional: 6424*(483-320)/803. The denominator is the entire poll, not only the winner’s supporters.
source_cases.check: 3864 estimates Cruz’s votes; 163 is the poll lead; 1304 estimates the election lead.

source_cases.title: Scale both fitted coefficients when all outputs scale
source_cases.spot: A second data set multiplies every y-coordinate by a fixed positive factor.
source_cases.hand: The original fitted line is approximately y=12+1.5x. Multiplying every output by 3.9 gives y=46.8+5.85x. Both the intercept and the slope scale; x is unchanged. Select the nearby model y=46.8+5.9x.
source_cases.calculator: Optional: 3.9*(12+1.5x), then distribute or compare 3.9*12 and 3.9*1.5. Do not refit invented data points.
source_cases.check: The new line passes approximately through (0,46.8) and (12,117). Scaling only the slope or only the intercept fails one of these checks.

source_cases.title: A truncated horizontal axis hides the true intercept
source_cases.spot: The plot starts near x=10; a choice incorrectly uses the visible left-edge height as the y-intercept.
source_cases.hand: Use points on the fitted line, approximately (12,480) and (24,880). The slope is about 400/12≈33. Then b=y-mx≈480-33*12=84. The intercept belongs at x=0, even when x=0 is not displayed.
source_cases.calculator: Optional: (880-480)/(24-12), then 480-33*12. Match the level of approximation used by the offered choices.
source_cases.check: The model d=33t+84 predicts 480 at t=12. A constant term 300 confuses the chart’s visible lower edge with the intercept.

source_cases.title: Average only the observed points meeting the input condition
source_cases.spot: A scatterplot statement gives an x-range and asks for the average of the corresponding y-values.
source_cases.hand: For widths between 18 and 48 cm, select the five observed boards at widths 24,24,30,36,42. Their prices are 10,15,20,30,40 dollars. The mean price is 115/5=23 dollars. Repeated x=24 marks two distinct boards.
source_cases.calculator: Optional: mean([10,15,20,30,40]). Do not average the widths or substitute points on an imagined fitted line.
source_cases.check: The subgroup with widths greater than 48 has a different mean, 63.75 dollars; changing the input filter changes the data being averaged.

source_cases.title: Percent of the input is linear; percent of the previous output is exponential
source_cases.spot: Both prompts mention percentages, but they apply the percent to different quantities.
source_cases.hand: “201% of x” means f(x)=2.01x, an increasing line. “Increases by 0.49% of its value the previous year” multiplies the previous output by 1.0049, an increasing exponential. Identify what the percent is taken of before choosing the model.
source_cases.calculator: Optional comparison: graph 2.01x and 1.0049^x using sensible windows. Model identification follows from the definition, not the appearance of one small graph window.
source_cases.check: A percentage word alone does not imply exponential change. The recurrence or fixed ratio between successive outputs is the distinguishing feature.

source_cases.title: Compare annual earnings rather than starting balances
source_cases.spot: One account starts smaller but compounds; another has a larger balance and fixed annual dollar growth.
source_cases.hand: Account A begins at 500 dollars and first earns 0.06*500=30 dollars. Later yearly interest exceeds 30 as its balance grows. Account B earns exactly 25 dollars each year. Therefore A earns more every year even though its initial balance is smaller.
source_cases.calculator: Optional: first-year earnings 0.06*500 versus 25. Comparing total balances alone would answer a different question.
source_cases.check: The conclusion concerns each year’s increase, not which account has the larger balance on a particular date.

source_cases.title: Use median, mean, and range together to recover endpoints
source_cases.spot: An ordered list contains unknown minimum, middle, and maximum values and gives three summary statistics.
source_cases.hand: Seven values make the fourth value b equal to median 29. A mean of 36 requires sum 252, giving a+c=90 after subtracting known values. Range 72 gives c-a=72. Add the equations to obtain 2c=162, so c=81 and a=9.
source_cases.calculator: Optional check: mean([9,26,29,29,31,47,81])=36; 81-9=72. No regression is involved.
source_cases.check: Check the recovered values preserve the stated ascending order. The range is a difference, not the maximum itself.

source_cases.title: Describe every possible output after eliminating an input
source_cases.spot: A system asks for all possible y-coordinates, rather than for one feasible point.
source_cases.hand: From 2x>5, x>5/2. From y>2x-1, x<(y+1)/2. Such an x exists exactly when 5/2<(y+1)/2, or y>4. This proves both that every solution has y>4 and that every y>4 can occur.
source_cases.calculator: Optional illustration: y=5 permits 2.5<x<3, so x=2.75 works. Boundary y=4 would require x>2.5 and x<2.5 simultaneously. These samples illustrate the exact interval argument.
source_cases.check: A necessary lower bound alone does not establish all possible values. Show the remaining input interval is nonempty for every output in the claimed set.

source_cases.title: Match the complete function input
source_cases.spot: A rule is stated as f(cx)=x-8, while a separate value is given at the input 2.
source_cases.hand: The output f(2)=35 means x-8=35, so the rule parameter x must be43. Its function input is then c*43=2, giving c=2/43. Equivalently set u=cx to obtain f(u)=u/c-8.
source_cases.calculator: Optional arithmetic: 2/(35+8). Verify the candidate by calculating 2/(2/43)-8=35. Define f(u)=u/(2/43)-8 only after solving the parameter relationship.
source_cases.check: The x in f(cx) is not the input itself. Substituting x=2 would evaluate f(2c), rather than the given f(2).

source_cases.title: Parameterize the entire common line
source_cases.spot: A system has equivalent equations and asks which point lies on both for every real parameter r.
source_cases.hand: Divide 28x+24y=20 by 4 to see that both equations are 7x+6y=5. Choose y=r and solve x=(5-6r)/7. Thus ((5-6r)/7,r) describes every point on the common line.
source_cases.calculator: Optional numeric checks: use r=0 and r=7, giving (5/7,0) and (-37/7,7). These checks reject incorrect choices; substitution 7((5-6r)/7)+6r=5 proves the family.
source_cases.check: The coordinate assigned to r matters. If x=r instead, y=(5-7r)/6. Do not read one graph intersection as the entire solution set.

source_cases.title: Eliminate an unknown compound term to recover a parameter
source_cases.spot: The system ax+by=72 and 6x+2by=56 intersects at (4,y), with a and b unknown.
source_cases.hand: Subtract twice the first equation from the second: (6-2a)x=-88. Insert the known x=4 to get 6-2a=-22 and a=14. Neither b nor the intersection y-coordinate is needed.
source_cases.calculator: Optional arithmetic: (56-2*72)/4=-22, then (6+22)/2=14. Sliders for both unknown coefficients add work and do not establish a unique answer.
source_cases.check: The premise guarantees a consistent intersection. Here by=-16, so b cannot be zero; graphing arbitrary b=0 would contradict the premise.

source_cases.title: A symbolic output offset cancels in the slope
source_cases.spot: A linear table contains a constant added to every output, or a common unknown shift in inputs.
source_cases.hand: For d4572f55, points (-34,t),(-17,t+23),(0,t+46) give slope ((t+23)-t)/17=23/17 and intercept t+46. For 3008cfc3 the input difference (k+7)-k=7 gives slope -4; moving five units back from (k,13) gives intercept output 33.
source_cases.calculator: Use numerical differences 23/17 or (-15-13)/7 after canceling the shared symbol by hand. A numeric regression cannot infer a unique symbolic offset from unspecified t.
source_cases.check: An arbitrary value of the offset is an illustration, not a proof for all offsets. The exact x=0 table row exposes the symbolic y-intercept.

source_cases.title: Treat repeated scaled quantities as whole unknowns
source_cases.spot: Equations repeat groups such as 8x and 7y, and the question asks for their combination.
source_cases.hand: Let u=8x and v=7y. Then 2u+4v=12 and -2u+4v=12. Adding gives 8v=24, so v=3; substitution gives u=0. The requested 8x+7y is u+v=3.
source_cases.calculator: Graph 2x+4y=12 and -2x+4y=12 only if x and y are explicitly relabeled as u and v; their intersection (0,3) is in grouped coordinates.
source_cases.check: A calculator point from the relabeled equations is not the original (x,y)=(0,3/7). Keep the variable definitions visible.

source_cases.title: A minimum count makes heavy items consume only the upgrade budget
source_cases.spot: At least 10 packages, each 100 or 120 pounds, must fit within 1100 pounds.
source_cases.hand: Ten light packages weigh 1000 pounds. Replacing one by a heavy package adds 20 pounds. The remaining 100 pounds allow five upgrades. Five heavy plus five light packages meet both bounds, so five heavy packages are attainable and maximal.
source_cases.check: The baseline argument needs nonnegative integer counts and must establish attainability. Dividing the total capacity by 120 alone ignores the minimum package count.

source_cases.title: Check a third constraint at the sole existing intersection
source_cases.spot: A graph of two intersecting lines is supplemented with a third linear equation.
source_cases.hand: The original two lines intersect only at(8,2). Any point satisfying all three must first satisfy those two, so(8,2) is the only candidate. The added equation x+4y=-16 fails there because8+4(2)=16, not-16. Thus the full system has zero solutions.
source_cases.calculator: Optional illustration: graph y=2, x+4y=16, and x+4y=-16. The original pair meet at(8,2); the third line misses that point. Direct substitution proves the failure without relying on plotted precision.
source_cases.check: Three pairwise intersections do not establish one common intersection. This shortcut assumes the original two equations have exactly one common point; coincident originals require another consistency check.

source_cases.title: Match the solution set rather than matching the original lines
source_cases.spot: A replacement system is requested to have the same solution as a graphed system.
source_cases.hand: The original lines intersect at(3/2,0). The very different equations x=3/2 and y=0 have exactly that one common solution, so they form a valid replacement system. Neither replacement equation needs to describe an original line.
source_cases.calculator: Optional: graph x=3/2 and y=0 to see their common point. Inspect the original graph independently before deciding that its intersection has the same coordinates.
source_cases.check: Matching a system solution is weaker than making each equation equivalent to an original equation. Preserve both coordinate order and the requirement that the replacement system has no additional solutions.

source_cases.title: Conserve the solute when the mixture volume changes
source_cases.spot: An unknown amount of one concentration is added to a known amount to reach a target concentration.
source_cases.hand: Let x be liters of25% solution added to3 liters of10% solution. Salt before mixing is0.25x+0.10(3); the final volume is x+3 and target salt is0.15(x+3). Equating these gives0.10x=0.15 and x=1.5 liters.
source_cases.calculator: Optional: graph y=0.25x+0.30 and y=0.15(x+3), reading x=1.5. Verify0.675/4.5=0.15 after solving.
source_cases.check: The final solution amount is x+3, not x. Concentration times volume measures the solute contribution under the stated mixture model; do not equate concentrations directly or average them without volume weights.

source_cases.title: Count only the units beyond the first price tier
source_cases.spot: The first fixed number of people, days, or hours has one price and later units have another.
source_cases.hand: For n museum visitors, the first25 cost21(25), and only n-25 cost14 each. Thus f(n)=525+14(n-25)=14n+175 on n>=25. Similarly, d rental days cost52+26(d-1); ten work hours cost8p+1.5p(10-8).
source_cases.calculator: Optional arithmetic: for26 visitors compute21*25+14*(26-25)=539. For two rental days compute52+26*(2-1)=78. Test the first-tier endpoint before trusting an expanded formula.
source_cases.check: Charging the second rate on every unit double-counts the tier already included. The constant175 is an adjustment in the expanded formula, not a real museum charge for zero visitors; the model has a restricted domain.

source_cases.title: Gluing removes two copies of the contact face
source_cases.spot: Two identical square-based prisms are joined at one base, and the new surface area is given as a fraction of one original surface area.
source_cases.hand: Write K=2s^2+360s for one height-90 prism. Joining two hides two square faces, so 2K-2s^2=(92/47)K. Hence K=47s^2; substitution gives 45s^2=360s and the positive solution s=8.
source_cases.calculator: Optional arithmetic check at s=8: K=2*8^2+360*8=3008; joined surface 2*3008-2*8^2=5888, which equals (92/47)*3008.
source_cases.check: The contact has two faces, one from each solid. The zero algebraic root is a collapsed prism and must be discarded.

source_cases.title: Recover vertical height from lateral surface area
source_cases.spot: A right square pyramid gives total surface area and combined lateral area but asks for its vertical height.
source_cases.hand: Base area=70560-38160=32400, so base side s=180. Each triangular face has area9540, giving slant height l=2*9540/180=106. The central vertical section has legs h and s/2=90, so h=sqrt(106^2-90^2)=56.
source_cases.calculator: Evaluate sqrt((2*(38160/4)/sqrt(70560-38160))^2-((sqrt(70560-38160))/2)^2), or compute the intermediate lengths separately to preserve meaning.
source_cases.check: A lateral face altitude is the slant height. The right triangle for vertical height uses half a base side, not the full side or half a diagonal.

source_cases.title: Follow a supplied volume formula for a tapered glass
source_cases.spot: A tapered glass has diameter and height labels in terms of k and supplies V=7pi*k^3/48.
source_cases.hand: Use the supplied frustum formula: 473=7pi*k^3/48, so k=(473*48/(7pi))^(1/3), approximately10.11 centimeters.
source_cases.calculator: Enter (473*48/(7*pi))^(1/3). Substitute each candidate into 7*pi*k^3/48 if checking choices numerically.
source_cases.check: The glass is neither a cylinder nor a complete cone. Its given formula already includes the taper; do not infer a replacement formula from its appearance.

source_cases.title: Two proportional sides with a nonincluded angle leave ambiguity
source_cases.spot: A proof question gives equal angles B=G=51 and AB=6, FG=18; statement III also sets FH=3AC.
source_cases.hand: I supplies A=F and II supplies C=H; either combines with B=G for AA similarity. III gives AB/FG=AC/FH=1/3, but B and G are not included between those side pairs, so it is SSA and is insufficient.
source_cases.calculator: Optional counterexample construction: set AC=5, AB=6 and scale FG=18,FH=15. The sine rule gives sin C=6*sin(51*pi/180)/5, allowing both an acute C and its obtuse supplement. Both leave a positive third angle, so choose different branches in the two triangles.
source_cases.check: The counterexample makes the insufficiency concrete: a failed named theorem alone is not a proof that no other constraint forces similarity.

source_cases.title: Separate the information needed for similarity and congruence
source_cases.spot: Intersecting segments supply vertical angles; statement I adds a second right angle, while II adds AC=DC=13.
source_cases.hand: I alone gives AA similarity but leaves a free size ratio. II alone gives one equal side and the vertical-angle pair but leaves a second angle free. Together they would give ASA congruence; the question asks about each statement by itself, so neither is sufficient.
source_cases.calculator: No graph is needed. For I, scale one right triangle by 2 to retain its angles while changing its sides. For II, vary the ray through D while preserving DC=AC and the common crossing angle.
source_cases.check: Read whether statements are tested separately or jointly. A fixed length must accompany enough angle or side information to force congruence.

source_cases.title: Count how many angles come from each of two measures
source_cases.spot: A transversal creates four angles of measure a and four of measure180-a, and the question asks for a sum of selected angles.
source_cases.hand: For fecc446d let a=7x-250 and b=430-7x. A sum of four angles must be ja+(4-j)b with integer j from0 to4. The five expressions are28x-1000,14x-320,360,-14x+1040,-28x+1720; -14x+1540 is absent. For f67255ea, (9x-560)+3(740-9x)=-18x+1660.
source_cases.calculator: Expand the five candidate expressions separately if helpful. To test identities numerically, choose an admissible x such as40 in fecc446d, making a30 and b150; all four-angle sums are120,240,360,480,600.
source_cases.check: The question asks for an identity for all admissible x. One accidental equality at a chosen x would not establish such an identity.

source_cases.title: Use a height inequality to list discrete similarity outputs
source_cases.spot: A right triangle has total base5+7, integer height y, area between48 and60 inclusive, and a smaller parallel height x.
source_cases.hand: Area=12y/2=6y, so8<=y<=10. The integer heights are8,9,10. Similarity gives x/y=5/12, producing x=10/3,15/4,25/6; any one answers the question.
source_cases.calculator: Evaluate 5*[8,9,10]/12 as a list, or compute the three fractions individually after the integer restriction is applied.
source_cases.check: The integrality applies to y, not x. Keep the inclusive endpoints and enter one allowed x rather than all possible values.

source_cases.title: Transfer an angle across an altitude before choosing a tangent
source_cases.spot: An altitude from the right-angle vertex creates smaller similar right triangles, and a trig ratio is asked at a differently named angle.
source_cases.hand: For603c18ad, WYX~XYZ with small angleX corresponding to large angleZ. Therefore tanZ=WY/WX=572/429=4/3 directly. For98e02472, the same angle matching gives a=b; sina=12/13 implies tanb=12/5.
source_cases.calculator: Optional:572/429 or12/sqrt(13^2-12^2). No inverse trig is needed; the angle correspondence must be established before using the ratio.
source_cases.check: At the original right-angle vertex the altitude splits the90-degree angle into two distinct acute angles. Label the smaller triangle whose sides form the chosen ratio.

source_cases.title: Turn an equal-length condition into a ratio of heights
source_cases.spot: An isosceles triangle contains a parallel cross section with midpointO, AO=BO, and angleOAC30 degrees.
source_cases.hand: Symmetry makes BF perpendicularAC. In AOF, let OF=x; the30-degree angle gives AO=2x, and the given equality gives BO=2x. Thus BF=3x. Similar BDE and BAC have scale BO/BF=2/3, so BE=(2/3)*BC=(2/3)*81=54.
source_cases.calculator: Only the final arithmetic81*(2/3)=54 is needed. An arbitrary coordinate plot can illustrate the geometry but does not replace the symmetry and special-triangle steps.
source_cases.check: BO is the smaller triangle height; BF is the full height. Use BO+OF for BF before transferring the ratio to the corresponding side.

source_cases.title: Find a triangle area from two sides and the included angle
source_cases.spot: Two known sides meet at a known angle, or a known leg and acute angle determine a perpendicular height.
source_cases.hand: For6c67dd47 take XY26 as base. The height is19sin54 degrees, giving area247sin54 degrees. For85f1892d, the other leg is26tan33 degrees, giving area338tan33 degrees; the question asks for the coefficient, so no trig evaluation is necessary.
source_cases.calculator: If a decimal is asked, use247*sin(54*pi/180) or338*tan(33*pi/180) in radian mode. For these exact expression/coefficient questions, keep the trig term symbolic.
source_cases.check: The sine-area formula uses the angle included between the two known sides. A side at an oblique angle is not itself the perpendicular height.

source_cases.title: Distinguish an equilateral triangle altitude from its circumradius
source_cases.spot: An equilateral triangle is inscribed in a circle, or a rectangle diagonal is twice its short side.
source_cases.hand: For54df8076 the side is852/3=284. Joining the circle center to a side midpoint gives a30-60-90 triangle with long leg142 and hypotenuse R, so R=284/sqrt3=(284/3)sqrt3. Thus w=284/3. For44b2b894, sides s and s*sqrt3 give area s^2*sqrt3=1089sqrt3, so s33 and diagonal/diameter66.
source_cases.calculator: Use852/9 for w, orsqrt1089*2 for the rectangle diameter. Keep the exact coefficient284/3 rather than rounding the radius before dividing bysqrt3.
source_cases.check: The equilateral circumradius is two-thirds of its altitude. The incircle radius is one-third of the altitude; these are different circles.

source_cases.title: Recover a parameter from a point on the resized circle
source_cases.spot: A circle equation contains n; a point lies on a concentric circle whose diameter is doubled.
source_cases.hand: Complete squares to(x-5)^2+(y-4)^2=14n+41. Double diameter means double radius, so the new squared radius is4(14n+41). Substitute(11,8):36+16=4(14n+41), giving n=-2.
source_cases.calculator: Evaluate((52/4)-41)/14=-2 and verify14*(-2)+41=13>0. Graphing both circles is optional after the parameter has been found.
source_cases.check: The supplied point belongs to circleB. Substituting it into the original circleA would solve a different problem. Check that the recovered squared radius is positive.

source_cases.title: Use the two congruent tangent triangles to recover length or area
source_cases.spot: Two tangents meet at a common exterior point; the question gives a perimeter or a center-to-exterior distance.
source_cases.hand: For0acfddb5, two radii168 and two equal tangents t give3856=336+2t, so t1760; the perpendicular radius gives center-to-exterior distance sqrt(168^2+1760^2)=1768. Forc0b53183, center distance510 and radius78 give tangent504. The quadrilateral is two right triangles, so its area is78*504=39312.
source_cases.calculator: Optional checks:sqrt(168^2+1760^2), then78*sqrt(510^2-78^2). Keep the distinction between the hypotenuse and the tangent visible.
source_cases.check: Equal tangents require the same exterior endpoint. The quadrilateral area is twice a half-product, so the final product has no factor1/2.

source_cases.title: Use squared distances for interior tests and axis tangency
source_cases.spot: A point is tested for being inside a circle, or a circle must meet an axis at exactly one point.
source_cases.hand: Foracd30391, center(-3,1) and r^2=25 make the squared-distance test(x+3)^2+(y-1)^2<25. At(3,2),37>25, so the point is outside. For9d159400, tangency to the y-axis requires |h|=r; center(4,9) and r4 qualify.
source_cases.calculator: Evaluate(3+3)^2+(2-1)^2=37 without taking a square root. Alternatively setx=0 in(x-4)^2+(y-9)^2=16 to get(y-9)^2=0, one solution.
source_cases.check: Interior uses strict inequality. Equality is the boundary. For tangency to the x-axis compare |k| with r; for the y-axis compare |h|.

source_cases.title: Conditional structures also occur outside the Probability skill
source_cases.spot: Each percentage names a smaller eligible group, or a table asks for a share within one employee.
source_cases.hand: Red-and-striped=.4×.3=.12 of all items. All three sessions:1250×.72×.36=324. Not green-rectangular-metal:1−.37×.37×.42=.942502, or94.2502%. Employee A one-star calls:16/145≈11%, not16/500 or16/50.
source_cases.calculator: Enter100*(1-.37*.37*.42) for the complement or100*16/145 for the table. Identify each denominator before typing.
source_cases.check: These are conditional multiplications, not independence assumptions. NOT(A and B and C) is the complement of the complete joint event, not NOT A and NOT B and NOT C.

source_cases.title: Compare unit rates before comparing the two options
source_cases.spot: Prices and protein quantities differ across foods.
source_cases.hand: Egg cost/protein=.36/6=.06 dollars/g; milk=.24/8=.03 dollars/g. Their ratio is2:1, not the raw-price ratio3:2.
source_cases.calculator: (.36/6)/(.24/8) returns2; hand division is shorter here.
source_cases.check: Keep both denominators. A cheaper package need not be cheaper per unit of the resource the question names.

source_cases.title: Enlarging a drawing shrinks the real distance per printed inch
source_cases.spot: A print is enlarged while representing the same actual region.
source_cases.hand: A65%longer drawing scales lengths by1.65. The old19miles now span1.65printed inches, so each new inch represents19/1.65≈11.52miles(B). The55-inch total side length cancels.
source_cases.calculator: 19/1.65. A graph adds unnecessary work.
source_cases.check: The drawing changes, not the real region. Distinguish miles per printed inch from printed inches per mile; area scaling would square the enlargement.

source_cases.title: Convert powers of units independently
source_cases.spot: Acceleration, area per time, or squared nautical miles.
source_cases.hand: 7.3m/s² becomes7.3×60²/1609≈16.3miles/min².250ft²/hour becomes250/(3.28²×60)≈.39m²/min.46nauticalmi² becomes46×1.852²≈157.8km².
source_cases.check: The exponent belongs to each unit separately. Squared time uses60², whereas ordinary hours-to-minutes uses60; square meters require squaring the length conversion.

source_cases.title: Substitute a shared ratio instead of finding its components
source_cases.spot: Two equations contain the same quotient and a new parameter.
source_cases.calculator: (6.7/4)/26.8 for the second source. Hand cancellation is quicker than solving for a and b separately.
source_cases.check: The component variables are not determined, and need not be. Retain nonzero denominator conditions; choosing a zero denominator destroys the ratio.

source_cases.title: A uniform quantity follows area shares, not side-length shares
source_cases.spot: Two squares share a uniform field, and total flux is known.
source_cases.hand: Side ratio3:1 gives area ratio9:1. Uniform field means flux has the same ratio, so the larger square receives9/10×4640=4176. Field strength29 cancels; there is no need to solve either area.
source_cases.check: Uniformity and equal orientation are essential. If strength or angle differed between squares, the simple area allocation would fail.

source_cases.title: New monthly cohorts differ from a shrinking balance
source_cases.spot: A repeated percentage refers either to a fresh equal monthly group or the previous remaining value.
source_cases.hand: Same1300000sales each month with15%returns for6months gives1300000×.15×6=1170000. A stove losing20%of its previous value each year instead gives800×.8²=512 after2years.
source_cases.check: Read the base anew each period. Repeated occurrences alone do not justify an exponential model; “previous year’s value” changes the base, while equal new sales do not.

source_cases.title: Recover the requested difference without first finding the whole
source_cases.spot: A known subgroup determines a missing total, but the requested output is another subgroup or difference.
source_cases.hand: Committee:students have15%and number6; teacher-minus-administrator share is45%−25%=20%. Thus6×.20/.15=8. Marbles:360remain after20%removal, so removed/remaining=.20/.80 and360×.20/.80=90.
source_cases.check: Match both shares to the same original whole. Applying20%to the remaining360 incorrectly changes the reference group.

c81b6c57.title: Two printed arithmetic errors; answer 7 remains correct
c81b6c57.text: The expansion repeats +24. The constant term is 24 only once. Matching x coefficients gives -13p-64=-155, so -13p=-91, not the printed -71, and p=7.

2c288148.title: Squaring requires a nonnegative right side
2c288148.text: For sqrt(k-x)=58-x, the valid sign condition is 58-x>=0. The printed strict >0 excludes the legitimate endpoint x=58, k=58. It does not change the minimum 4k=231.

5edc8c98.title: Factored expansion drops the leading coefficient on the constant term
5edc8c98.text: The source expands64(x-p)(x-q)=0 as64x²-64(p+q)x+pq=0. The final term must be64pq. The subsequent x-coefficient comparison and answer1/16 remain correct, as does the alternate derivation.
5edc8c98.entry: Use64x²-64(p+q)x+64pq=0. Compare x-coefficients to obtain p+q=(16a+4b)/64=(4a+b)/16.

85939da5.title: A margin of error does not make interval values equally likely
85939da5.text: The official explanation correctly forms 27%–33% from 30% ± 3 percentage points, but then says any value in that interval is equally likely. The margin of error alone supplies no uniform probability distribution over the population percentage. The keyed answer D, that 35% is doubtful, remains the intended conclusion.
85939da5.entry: Use the interval as a range of plausible population percentages; do not assign equal probabilities to its points or say values outside it are impossible.

6a305cd0.title: The interval is plausible, not guaranteed
6a305cd0.text: The official rationale says the population mean “will fall” between 34 and 40. A sample mean of 37 with margin 3 supports that interval as plausible; it does not guarantee coverage. Choice C is the intended best answer. The explanations for choices A and B also discuss values below 34 or above 40, although the printed choices compare with 37.
6a305cd0.entry: Read C as the plausible interval 37 ± 3 = [34,40]. Neither a direction from 37 nor exact certainty follows.

203774bc.title: Middle-term split has reversed signs
203774bc.text: The source rewrites 2y²+11y-546 as 2y²+28y-39y-546, whose middle coefficient is -11. The next factorization is correct for the original polynomial; the split must instead be -28y+39y. The key 14 remains correct.
203774bc.entry: Use 2y²-28y+39y-546=2y(y-14)+39(y-14)=(2y+39)(y-14). Positive integer y=14 and x=39.

00165291.title: Equal root equations do not imply equal selected roots
00165291.text: The alternate rationale says that a is equal to c because 2a²-31a+105=0 and 2c²-31c+105=0 represent the same equation. This implication is false: a and c may be different roots, and the given integer/noninteger conditions require a=5 and c=21/2. The answer 15.5 and primary derivation are correct.
00165291.entry: Both parameters belong to the root set {5,21/2}. Select a=5 using integrality and c=21/2 using nonintegrality, then add.

4e18fc5d.title: Positivity conditions contradict the equation
4e18fc5d.text: The source states that v, w, and x are distinct positive numbers, but v=-w/(150x) is negative whenever w and x are positive. Thus no triple satisfies all conditions. The formal rearrangement w=-150vx (choice A) is algebraically correct.
4e18fc5d.entry: Multiply by -150x for x nonzero to obtain w=-150vx. Flag the inconsistent positivity premise rather than silently treating it as satisfiable.

22fd3e1f.title: Distractor check uses an excluded input
22fd3e1f.text: The source rejects choice A by evaluating at x=0 although the question restricts x>3. The answer D is correct; the counterexample should respect the stated domain.
22fd3e1f.entry: Factor and cancel x-3 only for allowed inputs. At x=4, the original expression and D equal28/5 whereas A equals1/5.

29ed5d39.title: Rationale solves a different equation
29ed5d39.text: The question gives p=20+16/n with p>20, but the entire source derivation uses p=9+14/n and p>9. Choice D remains correct for the actual question.
29ed5d39.entry: Subtract20 to obtain p-20=16/n, multiply by nonzero n, and divide by positive p-20: n=16/(p-20).

c6e85cd7.title: Incorrect decimal entry example
c6e85cd7.text: The exact answer7/24 and main exponent derivation are correct, but the source lists0.219 as a valid answer. It is not a rounding or truncation of7/24.
c6e85cd7.entry: Equate exponents8c=7/3, so c=7/24≈0.2916667. Use7/24 or an appropriately rounded decimal.

2d1614a1.title: Distractor explanation changes the growth interval
2d1614a1.text: The main solution correctly identifies factor1.04 every18months from exponent(2/3)t, but the choice B explanation incorrectly says the factor1.04 applies each year.
2d1614a1.entry: Over18months=3/2years the exponent increases by1, hence4% growth per18months. The annual factor is1.04^(2/3).

b73ee6cf.title: Distractor explanation calls a decay impossible
b73ee6cf.text: Choice A is50,000=60,000(0.03)^t. Its explanation says decreasing from60,000 to50,000 is impossible given the growth factor. This equation actually uses a decay factor0.03 and does have a positive time solution; it simply models the wrong initial value, direction, and rate. The correct answer D is unchanged.
b73ee6cf.entry: Use target=initial*(1+rate)^time:60,000=50,000(1.03)^t. Reject A because it describes97% decay starting at60,000.

08d03fe4.title: Displayed forms are not equivalent and rationale changes the base
08d03fe4.text: The original question image labels50*2^(x+1),80*2^x,128*2^(x-1),205*2^(x-2) as equivalent forms. Their values atx=1 are200,160,128,102.5, so that premise is false. The rationale instead uses128*(1.6)^(x-1). C still displays its own valuef(1)=128 as coefficient.
08d03fe4.entry: Read C atx=1:128*2^0=128. Flag the inconsistent equivalence premise and base mismatch; do not silently rewrite the source forms.

1e11190a.title: The berry calculation gives B, despite the rationale label C
1e11190a.text: The original question lists B as 5 pints and C as 8 pints. The rationale correctly computes 5 pints of blackberries but labels the answer C and rejects B. It also calls D the raspberry count, although the system gives 4 pints of raspberries (A), not 12 (D). The committed and uploaded PDF answer keys correctly give B.
1e11190a.entry: Use r=4 and b=5: 5.50(4)+3(5)=37 and 6.50(4)+8(5)=66. The requested blackberry count is 5, choice B.

153ee763.title: Check the zero coefficient before dividing
153ee763.text: The original rationale divides x(1-7p)=-28 by 1-7p and then calls the resulting quotient equation false when 1-7p=0. That quotient is undefined there, and the division is not equivalent at that parameter. The final answer 1/7 is correct.
153ee763.entry: Keep (-3+21p)x=84. Set -3+21p=0 to get p=1/7; the original equation then reads 0=84, so no x works.

ee7b1de1.title: The candle solution has a subtraction typo before the correct bound
ee7b1de1.text: The original rationale correctly obtains 980+6.70l<=2200, then says subtracting 980 gives 6.70l<=2200. The right side should be 1220. The following bound l<=182.09 and final answer 182 use the correct subtraction.
ee7b1de1.entry: Compute (2200-980)/6.70=182.0895...; 182 large and 18 small candles cost 2199.40 dollars. 183 large with at least 17 small cost 2206.10 dollars.

bf5f80c6.title: The worked coordinates establish A, despite the rationale label D
bf5f80c6.text: The original question asks which point satisfies y<-4x+4. Choice A is (-4,0), and 0<20 is true. Choice D is (2,-1), and -1<-4 is false. The original rationale says choice D but correctly checks (-4,0), then incorrectly rejects A. The committed answer and uploaded PDF key are A and are correct; this is a rationale answer-letter mismatch.
bf5f80c6.entry: Substitute each candidate into the inequality. A: 0<20 is true. B: 5<4 is false. C: 1<-4 is false. D: -1<-4 is false.

71189542.title: The 38 is a deficit of people, not a count of tents
71189542.text: The alternate explanation says “each of these 38 tents” after calculating a 38-person capacity deficit. The correct calculation immediately following it divides 38 by 2 to obtain 19 two-person tents. The answer C and the main elimination solution are correct.
71189542.entry: Read the deficit as 38 people. Each replacement of a four-person tent by a two-person tent removes two places, so 38/2=19 tents.

64c85440.title: The intended parking interval assumes the curb is fully allocated
64c85440.text: The official solution obtains 15 through 18 spaces by dividing the 135-foot curb by the permitted widths 9 through 7.5 feet. The lower bound 15 uses an implicit full-use assumption: if unused curb were allowed, fewer than 15 spaces could also be placed. Read D under the intended full-curb layout.
64c85440.entry: For a layout allocating all 135 feet to n equal-width standard spaces, 7.5<=135/n<=9 gives 15<=n<=18, with integer n.

daad7c32.title: The reverse spring rate is not the variable w
daad7c32.text: The original rationale correctly selects D: the spring length increases 2 centimeters per newton. Its explanation of distractor C says this describes the value w. In fact C describes the reverse rate, the increase in weight per centimeter, which is 1/2 newton per centimeter. The variable w is the weight itself. The answer D is unchanged.
daad7c32.entry: For L=30+2w, delta L/delta w=2 cm/N. Solving w=(L-30)/2 gives delta w/delta L=1/2 N/cm.

a1fd2304.title: The mixture equation conserves salt, not total solution volume
a1fd2304.text: The original rationale calls volume times concentration the total amount of saline solution. Those products measure the salt contribution; total solution volume is x+3 liters. The subsequent salt-balance equation and answer 1.5 liters are correct.
a1fd2304.entry: Use 0.10(3)+0.25x=0.15(3+x). For x=1.5, salt contributions sum to0.675, equal to0.15(4.5); the mixture volume is4.5 liters.

81b664bc.title: Use parallel intercepts; the adjacent trapezoids need not be similar
81b664bc.text: The original PDF rationale says AFEB and BEDC are similar because AF, BE, and CD are parallel. Parallel bases alone do not establish similarity of these quadrilaterals. The stated ratio and answer 17.5 are valid by the parallel intercept theorem applied to transversals AC and FD.
81b664bc.entry: The three parallel segments cut proportional consecutive lengths on the two transversals: AB/BC=FE/ED. Thus ED=18.5*8.5/9=17.4722..., which rounds to 17.5. No trapezoid similarity is required.

7268586c.title: The known angles add to 156, not 152
7268586c.text: The original rationale changes x+132+24=180 to x+152=180 and then reports x=24. The intermediate sum should be 156. The answer D, 24, and the alternate isosceles base-angle proof are correct.
7268586c.entry: Compute x=180-(132+24)=180-156=24. Alternatively PQ=QR makes the base angles P and R equal, so x=24 directly.

933fee1a.title: The right angle is C; B is the 58-degree angle
933fee1a.text: The first rationale sentence says the measure of angle B is 90 degrees while concluding that B must be 58 degrees. The diagram marks C as the right angle. Replacing B by C in the 90-degree statement restores the angle-sum argument. The selected ratio and answer B are correct.
933fee1a.entry: A=32 and C=90 imply B=58. In the other triangle D=58 and F=90 imply E=32. Matching opposite-32-degree legs and hypotenuses gives BC/AB=DF/DE.

2d31caae.title: The rejection of A describes the correct conditional percentage
2d31caae.text: The key B is correct: Employee A has16 one-star calls out of145, about11%. The rationale describes choice A as the percentage of Employee A’s calls that received one star, which is actually B’s quantity. A≈3% instead comes from16/500, using all employees’ calls. D=32% reverses the condition, using16/50. The source image is preserved.

d89c1513.title: A table column total is misprinted
d89c1513.text: The beverage cells are 60 and 35, totaling 95; the printed column total says 90. The four interior cells sum to the stated grand total of 135. The requested no-gas probability uses the unaffected row total 50/135, so key D remains correct. Use the interior cells to check inconsistent margins before choosing a denominator.

efc469c4.text: A sum of coefficients is the polynomial at 1. Match any outside scale before evaluating.

a255ae72.text: Substitute into the smallest repeated block before expanding.

77c0cced.text: One intersection means a repeated zero of the difference of the two equations.

02060533.text: Recover the requested function before reading its intercept.
02060533.entry: Multiply each table output g(x) by x+3. The recovered f values lie on f(x)=4x+36.

555939d2.text: Although filed under ratios/rates, the structure is inference from a sample. Scale8/300 to30000;800 is an estimate, not a census count.

3638f413.text: FromJanuary2001 toJanuary2005 there are four doublings. Reverse the exponential multiplier, not a linear annual increment.

3ac09984.text: Convert pesos to dollars, then retain98% after the fee on the converted amount.

8cbf1415.text: The30% striped share is conditional on being red. Multiply.4 by.3 for the joint share; this does not assume independent features.

34f8cd89.text: Multiply nested eligible shares, then subtract the whole joint event from1. “Not rectangular green metal” is not three simultaneous negative requirements.

eqx-coef: The requested sum equals 6f(1), not f(1); 6[-14*9+6*4]=-612.
eqx-rewrite: Subtract first: x²-y²=b-c; then square to b²-2bc+c².
nle-system: Subtract line from parabola: 2x²-24x+64-a has repeated root at x=6; original parabola vertex 21/4 is not the tangency x.
nle-count: b²-2704<0 and b positive integer give b<52; greatest 51.
nlf-exp: h(0)=10 gives b=9 since a>0 and a^0=1. Then a²=4 and a>0 gives a=2, so ab=18. The positive-base assumption excludes -2.

probability_review.scope: 49 question and solution OCR reviews, with ambiguous figures checked visually. These editorial groups do not predict future-test frequencies. No repeated-draw/replacement/binomial family was identified.
